entries.issuing_body: Nevada Gaming Control Board / Carson City District Court
entries.title: KalshiEX and Nevada Gaming Control Board file joint stipulation cancelling contempt hearing; Kalshi must implement GeoComply geofencing by August 12 or face $120,000/day fine
entries.facts: On July 24, 2026, KalshiEX LLC and the Nevada Gaming Control Board filed a joint stipulation order in Carson City District Court cancelling the pending contempt hearing. Under the stipulation, Kalshi must implement a GeoComply third-party geolocation solution to block Nevada users from accessing sports, election, and entertainment event contracts by August 12, 2026. Failure to meet the August 12 deadline results in a court-imposed fine of $120,000 per day. NGCB Chair Mike Dreitzer stated: 'This agreement will ensure that Kalshi fully complies with Nevada law moving forward, or it will face stiff penalties.' The NGCB made the joint stipulation public on July 25, 2026. Per the same reporting, Kalshi is also implementing GeoComply in Michigan with an August 12 compliance deadline.
entries.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, DCM operators, and gaming compliance teams operating in Nevada or facing state court geofencing orders

entries.title: Pennsylvania HB 2711 introduced: bipartisan bill proposes regulatory framework for prediction markets with AG enforcement authority, no ban, no revenue tax; referred to House committee
entries.facts: On July 22, 2026, Pennsylvania Representative Tarik Khan and 24 bipartisan co-sponsors (20 Democrats, 4 Republicans) introduced HB 2711 to amend Title 4 of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes. The bill would create a regulatory framework for prediction markets with enforcement authority vested in the Pennsylvania Attorney General and local district attorneys (not the Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board), a 21-year minimum age requirement, self-exclusion requirements, bans on death markets and contracts involving high school sports or minor participants, and civil penalties of up to $1 million per day for post-injunction violations. The bill does not prohibit most sports prediction markets and does not impose a revenue tax. HB 2711 was referred to the House Consumer Protection, Technology and Utilities Committee on July 22, 2026.
entries.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms considering Pennsylvania entry or monitoring state legislative developments in the prediction-markets space
